 Elina Svitolina has long tied her happiness to other people. At Wimbledon in 2023, she spoke about the “little happiness” she could offer people back home in Ukraine. A year later, she reached the quarter-finals on the same day a missile struck a children’s hospital in Kyiv. She then admitted to feeling guilty about celebrating her achievements while so much suffering continued around her. As the situation in Ukraine remained unchanged, the emotional toll gradually caught up with her, leaving her feeling as though she was losing herself — a struggle that also contributed to her separation from Gaël Monfils. The criticism that followed only added to the strain. So, ahead of the WTA Finals, her first tournament since announcing their separation, Svitolina was asked about the year she had endured, and her answer on happiness was blunt. 
 Watch What’s Trending Now!
 “For me, there’s no such thing as, probably, a general happy life because of the things that I have on a daily basis,” she said during the pre-tournament press conference at the WTA Finals . “But the happy moments that I can create with the people around me — it’s things that I can control and live with.”
 ADVERTISEMENT
 The Ukrainian also highlighted that constant public scrutiny has only made things more difficult, considering that people don’t hesitate before judging or commenting on her every move.
 “Yeah, as you mention, I’ve had a tough year with different things in my head. Very busy year that we have. Living in the public eye is not an easy task. Everything is just up there for people to judge or to comment on. Also, I would say it’s a difficult thing to have,” she added.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Svitolina initially cited the heavy psychological toll of the war in Ukraine as the reason behind her separation from Monfils — who, she said, saw all of it and “never let go of my hand.” But “some battles happen deep inside you,” and nobody else’s love can win them for you. 
 Svitolina had already cut her 2025 season short for related reasons. Citing psychological exhaustion and emotional fatigue, partly from the war, she wrote on Instagram at the time, “I haven’t been feeling like myself lately,” and said she needed space “to heal and recharge.” Yet, her decision drew backlash, with critics reading it as pinning the split on the war. The 32-year-old then gave a follow-up statement , clarifying that her decision involved much more than just the war and that she was no longer truly happy.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Monfils stepped in with a social media post on October 24. He wrote that Svitolina did not owe anyone an explanation but chose to speak “vulnerably and truthfully,” only for many to decide it “wasn’t perfect enough.” The criticism that followed was, in his words, “unkind at best and venomous at worst.” He called the lack of kindness shown to her upsetting and asked people to remember that much of what happens in a relationship cannot be explained in a post.
 “Elina and I may no longer be a couple, but we are still a family,” he wrote, adding that his heart hurts but he is grateful for her support and love over the years. Each of them has battles to fight, he said, and they will keep caring for each other as parents of a shared child.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 This whole saga has affected the two equally. The Frenchman abruptly retired shortly before the split became public. He said in October 2025 that 2026 would be his final season and had planned to bow out at the Paris Masters. Instead, in early October, he removed himself from the International Tennis Integrity Agency’s anti-doping pool, which made him ineligible to compete, and appeared on its retired list without any explanation. 
 He then pulled out of his last scheduled tournaments, including Paris. Both Monfils and Svitolina have since confirmed that the separation was behind the sudden exit. He later admitted that getting separated from Svitolina affected him deeply, and it even resulted in him not being able to follow his daily routines. 
 ADVERTISEMENT
 “The breakup with Elina hurt me deeply. We’re human, we have our own problems, and we don’t necessarily control what we want,” he said during a Twitch livestream. “This breakup didn’t leave me unaffected. For people who have been in my situation, going through a breakup isn’t easy, and when it happens, I can’t train the way I want, I’m not at my best psychologically. I’m not going to pretend. I’m eating less. I’m not doing everything as well.”
 Monfils still got a farewell in Paris on November 3, though not the one he had planned. His father, Rufin, attended, while his mother, Sylvette, stayed home to look after Skai. Svitolina was not reported to be there. He dedicated the night to Skai, saying the four-year-old had told him, “You don’t talk about me enough.” He also pointed out that November 3 was exactly eight years since he and Skai’s mother got together.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 But a day after the ceremony, Monfils wrote in French: “I’ll be honest with you: I was scared to come. The last few weeks have been full of emotions, and I didn’t dare to come find you.” 
 With his playing days now behind him, Monfils has been named France’s team captain for the Davis Cup. The FFT announced the appointment on Saturday, November 7. Monfils takes over from Paul-Henri Mathieu, who held the job for three years and led France to the quarter-finals in 2025. He called it “a great source of pride” and said the blue jersey “represents so much” to him.
 On the other hand, Svitolina returned to the court for the first time since her divorce. However, things didn’t quite go as planned.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Elina Svitolina suffered a crushing defeat 
 Svitolina had a dismal start to the year-end tournament as Andreeva defeated her 6-4, 6-0 in just 70 minutes. While the first set was pretty evenly matched, Andreeva swept past Svitolina in the second. The latter created six break-point opportunities, but wasn’t able to capitalize on any of them. In comparison, Andreeva converted four of the six break-point opportunities she got and took a 2-1 lead in the H2H record.
 The result now leaves the Ukrainian in the danger zone, and she will be up against Karolina Muchova next, who suffered a 7-6, 7-5 defeat to Aryna Sabalenka in her first match. 
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Despite leading Muchová 3-1 in their head-to-head record, Svitolina enters their upcoming clash as the underdog, with bookmakers favouring the Czech.
